media_strategy.selection_principle: default to all five channels (chart, image, video, audio, interactive_or_map); each channel chosen and executed in a data-driven way; skipping any channel requires an explicit reason in media_decisions

chart.reason: The dataset is a multi-decade quantitative trend on a log scale; charts are the core medium.

image.reason: Two archival reference photos exist (Gordon Moore, Intel 4004); we generate a cinematic teaser and an editorial pencil-line illustration to anchor the human side of the story.

video.reason: Disk space at runtime fell to <500MB, blocking video generation. The teaser is rendered as a still + slow CSS Ken-Burns animation to capture motion without an .mp4.

audio.reason: The dataset is purely tabular silicon counts. There is no embedded music or recorded performance, and sonifying a monotone log-exponential would map to a single rising tone that adds no signal beyond the chart.

interactive_or_map.reason: (1) Master scatter chart with hover tooltips for every chip; (2) guess-first slider for the 1965 Moore prediction. Together these turn the Moore-line claim into something the reader tests rather than reads.

media_blockers.reason: Disk fell below 500MB during the run; image2video and text2video skipped to avoid stalling.
A third generated image (modern die_macro.png) failed and disk was at 97%; skipped rather than retried.

des_01.label: Teaser — single silicon wafer in cleanroom

content.prompt: Cinematic macro photograph of a single silicon wafer reflecting blue and gold light in a dark cleanroom...

des_01.brief: Full-bleed cinematic still with subtle CSS Ken-Burns zoom and parallax. Headline 'A pencil line, drawn in 1975' fades in over the lower third on scroll.
des_01.rationale: Empirical-abstract dataset; the teaser earns engagement by giving the reader a tactile thing to anchor the upcoming numbers to. Still + CSS animation also avoids the failed video path.

des_02.label: Headline stat callout — 2.03 vs 2.00

content.label: years per doubling — empirical CPU rate, 1971-2019. Moore predicted 2.00.

des_02.brief: Oversize 96px serif numeral '2.03' with smaller label below; faint '/ 2.00 predicted' marker beside it.
des_02.rationale: The thesis is one number's near-equality with another. Lead with that.

des_03.label: Master scatter — every chip, log scale, with the Moore line

content.interaction: hover any point for chip name, year, family, transistor count; faint dashed Moore line overlaid

des_03.brief: Visual centrepiece. ~720px content width; X 1963-2019, Y log 1 to 200B. All 326 chips as small circles by family. Two highlight markers labelled: Intel 4004 (1971, 2,250) lower-left, AMD EPYC Rome (2019, 32B) upper-right. Moore's 1971-anchored 2-year line drawn faintly behind the points. Hover tooltip {chip, family, year, tc}. Legend top-right.
des_03.rationale: Headline chart: the prediction line and the cloud of points cohabit the same neighbourhood for 49 years.

des_04.label: Reference photo — Gordon Moore
des_04.brief: Floats left at ~280px width within the section column. Caption: 'Gordon Moore, around the time of the 1965 Electronics article.'
des_04.rationale: The 'man and the curve' section needs the man.

des_05.label: Reference photo — Intel 4004
des_05.brief: Floats right at ~280px width, paired with des_04. Caption: 'Intel 4004, 1971 — 2,300 transistors. The leftmost dot on every Moore's-Law plot.'
des_05.rationale: Anchor point of the entire CPU dataset.

des_06.label: Three-family race chart — CPU vs GPU vs RAM per-year max

content.interaction: hover for year + count; per-family doubling-time annotations near line endpoints

des_06.brief: Three roughly parallel lines on a log y axis (1 to 200B). Annotate each line with its doubling time near its endpoint: 'CPU 2.03 yr', 'GPU 1.85 yr', 'RAM 1.56 yr'.
des_06.rationale: Slopes are the story; small differences on a log scale matter.

des_07.label: Era-split chart: pre-2005 vs post-2005 doubling time
des_07.brief: Four bars: CPU pre-2005 (2.02), CPU 2005+ (2.51), GPU pre-2005 (1.62), GPU 2005+ (2.53). Reference horizontal line at 2.00 (Moore's prediction). Bars labelled with doubling time + CAGR.
des_07.rationale: The 2005 break is the key negative finding; bar chart makes the slowdown unmissable.

des_08.label: Hand-drawn pencil line — chapter break image

content.prompt: An abstract editorial illustration: a hand-drawn pencil line on graph paper, climbing diagonally upward...

des_08.brief: Inserted as a chapter break before the 'Where Moore was wrong' turn. ~720px wide, centered, vintage paper feel.
des_08.rationale: The 'where Moore was wrong' section needs a visual that cues 'forecast' rather than 'data'.

des_09.label: Guess the 1975 prediction — interactive reveal

content.initial_state: Horizontal log axis from 1,000 to 200,000 transistors with a draggable marker. Prompt: 'Moore predicted 65,000 components by 1975. Where did real chips actually land?'
content.trigger: Reader drags the marker and clicks 'Reveal'
content.transition: Two markers appear: faded grey at 65,000 (Moore), teal at 5,000 (real 1975 max). Text panel slides in: 'Moore overshot by 13x. He halved the doubling rate the same year, and the new line aged into a law.'
content.payoff: Reader feels the 1965 overshoot before reading the explanation

des_09.brief: Horizontal slider on a log scale. Reader drags marker, then 'Reveal' button shows Moore's 65K prediction and actual 1975 max (5K) side by side. Vanilla JS + range input + SVG markers; touch-friendly.
des_09.rationale: The 1965 overshoot lands harder if the reader commits to a guess first.

des_10.label: Residual chart — over-line and under-line CPUs/GPUs

content.interaction: hover for chip name + actual transistor count

des_10.brief: Scatter of top 5 over- and under-performers per family (~20 points). Y = log10 residual. Zero line emphasised. Itanium 2 family + SPARC64 above; ARM family + Atom below. Each point labelled with chip name.
des_10.rationale: Explicit residual chart with zero line makes the over/under split visible.

des_11.label: Milestones strip — 7 power-of-ten crossings

content.interaction: click a milestone for chip name + year

des_11.brief: Horizontal axis 1971-2019 with 8 ticks at the years each power-of-ten was first crossed. Labels alternate sides. Each tick caption: threshold + chip.
des_11.rationale: Compact rhythm visual between paragraphs; doesn't need a full chart.

des_12.label: Moore line vs actual CPU max — overlay chart

content.interaction: hover at any year shows predicted vs actual values and ratio

des_12.brief: Two overlaid lines: Moore's predicted CPU count (dashed grey, anchored at 1971's 2,300 with 2-year doubling) + actual CPU max per year (solid blue). Annotation at 2019: 'predicted 38.6B / actual 32B / 21% overshoot'.
des_12.rationale: Closing-loop chart: the reader sees prediction and data on the same axes.

des_13.label: After-the-dataset comparison — 4 stat callouts

content.label: Intel 4004 (1971) → AMD EPYC Rome (2019, dataset cutoff) → Apple M1 Ultra (2022) → Cerebras WSE-3 (2024). The dataset ends, the curve does not.

des_13.brief: Four small callout cards in a row: '2,300 — Intel 4004 (1971)', '32B — AMD EPYC Rome (2019, in dataset)', '114B — Apple M1 Ultra (2022, after)', '4T — Cerebras WSE-3 (2024, after)'. Final two cards faded to signal 'beyond this dataset'.
des_13.rationale: Stat callouts let the reader exit on the open question without another chart.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial, slightly archival — silver/blue/copper accents on near-black background, serif headlines, system-ui body, subtle paper texture in chapter breaks
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first at hook (full-bleed teaser + 96px stat callout); alternating prose-then-chart for the body; chapter-break image and interactive turn before the closing overlay chart; stat callouts at exit
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No three charts in a row: between des_06 and des_07 the reader gets a chapter-break image (des_08) plus the guess-the-prediction interactive (des_09), then the closing line overlay (des_12) and stat callouts (des_13). Avoids the standard chart-chart-chart cadence.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Headline serif at ~64px, section headers at ~32px, body 18px Georgia/serif. Stat numerals 96px in tabular figures. Subtle copper underline accents on key terms. No drop caps.
